name: suricata_run
description: Run a local Suricata rules file over a capture offline and record what ran: the engine's version (suricata --build-info, kept whole), the configuration with its SHA-256, the rules file's SHA-256, size and rule-line count, the checksum mode and the command. By default the tool writes an explicit suricata.yaml into out_dir (eve-log types by name with tls extended, the TLS fingerprint settings by key; nothing addressed by list position; everything it does not set is the engine's own default, not your distribution's suricata.yaml) or uses `config`, a local file of yours (never one from inputs/). The configuration is tested with `suricata -T` BEFORE the run; if that fails nothing is run and the diagnostic is returned whole. Rule-load numbers are read from Suricata's own output when it prints them (None is not zero) and a rule that failed to load fails the run. JA3/JA4 are three separate numbers: what the configuration asks for, the TLS events logged (the traffic that could carry a fingerprint) and the events that carry one; none is evidence about what the build supports. EVE lines that are not JSON, not objects or without an event_type are counted with their line numbers. eve.json is the whole result; inline alerts are bounded. An alert is a rule match, not a finding, and no ruleset ships with the pack. SENSITIVE: EVE can carry URLs, host names, SNI, DNS names and file names. The directory is private (0700/0600, Suricata's own files too); run it as a job with secret_output: true.

rules.description: A local Suricata rules file, passed with -S so only it is loaded; nothing is downloaded

out_dir.description: An empty directory under work/ (in a job, under $OUT) for eve.json, Suricata's logs, the configuration and the build information. It is private (0700, files 0600)

config.description: A local suricata.yaml of your own, used instead of the one this tool writes (default: the tool writes one). A configuration from inputs/ is refused. It is tested with -T before the run, and its fingerprint settings are not read

return_alerts.description: Alerts returned inline (default 100, 0 for none); every alert remains in eve.json and alerts_omitted says how many were left out

checksum_mode.description: none (default, tolerates capture-offload checksums) or all (validate every packet checksum); passed as -k and recorded

timeout_seconds.description: Kill the run, and everything it started, after this long (default 900, at least 10); the configuration test has its own 120 seconds
